correctness.rationale: Invariant averaging of x, y and x^2/2 gives E[y]=E[z]=E[xy]=0. Averaging the z equation then yields a quadratic in the mean m plus (33/100)Var(x) and (5/2)E[z erf(z)], whose latter two terms are nonnegative. Factoring the quadratic by the equilibrium roots proves the defect identity and excludes Delta<0; conversely Delta>=0 supplies an equilibrium compact invariant set. At Delta=0 or an endpoint mean, vanishing of all nonnegative terms fixes x and z, and the xy test fixes y. The midpoint mixture of equilibrium atoms attains the sharp variance bound, while any non-equilibrium ergodic measure is strict. Fresh symbolic algebra independently reproduced the discriminant factorization and the hidden-parameter constants.
